verses.sanskrit:
लोमश उवाच।
              सा तु नाव्याश्रमं चक्रे राजकार्यार्थसिद्धये। संदेशाच्चैव नृपतेः स्वबुद्ध्या चैव भारत॥१॥
verses.english: Lomasha said: O descendant of Bharata, in order to accomplish the king's works, she made a floating hermitage, both because the king ordered it and because it agreed with her opinion.

verses.sanskrit: नानापुष्पफलैर्वृक्षैः कृत्रिमैरुपशोभितैः। नानागुल्मलतोपेतैः स्वादुकामफलप्रदैः॥२॥
verses.english: She made that floating hermitage charming, extraordinary, magical extremely beautiful, exceedingly delightful, abounding in various plants and creepers, adorned with many artificial trees full of flowers and fruits and capable of giving various delicious fruits.

verses.sanskrit: अतीव रमणीयं तदतीव च मनोहरम्। चक्रे नाव्याश्रमं रम्यमद्भुतोपमदर्शनम्॥३॥
ततो निबध्य तां नावमदूरे काश्यपाश्रमात्। चारयामास पुरुषैर्विहारं तस्य वै मुनेः॥४॥
verses.english: Thereupon she moored that boat near the hermitage of Kashyapa's son and the sent men to survey the place which the Rishi generally frequented.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दुहितरं वेश्यां समाधायेतिकार्यताम्। दृष्ट्वान्तरं काश्यपस्य प्राहिणोद्बुद्धिसंमताम्॥५॥
verses.english: Then seeing an opportunity and having conceived a plan in her mind, she sent for her daughter, a courtesan, who was exceedingly clever. She then sent her to the son of Kashyapa.

verses.sanskrit: सा तत्र गत्वा कुशला तपोनित्यस्य संनिधौ। आश्रमं तं समासाद्य ददर्श तमृषेः सुतम्॥६॥
verses.english: That clever woman went near the ascetic arriving at the hermitage she saw the Rishi's son.
verses.bhavadeepa: समाधाय बोधयित्वा । इतिकार्यताम् इतिकर्तव्यताम् । अन्तरम् असान्निध्यम् ॥५॥

verses.sanskrit:
वेश्योवाच।
              कच्चिन्मुने कुशलं तापसानां कच्चिच्च वो मूलफलं प्रभूतम्। कच्चिद्भवान्रमते चाश्रमेऽस्मिंस्त्वां वै द्रष्टुं सांप्रतमागतोऽस्मि॥७॥
verses.english: The Courtesan said : O Rishi, I hope it all well with the ascetics here; I hope fruits and roots are plentiful here; I hope take delight in this hermitage. I have come to pay you a visit.

verses.sanskrit: कच्चित्तपो वर्धते तापसानां पिता च ते कच्चिदहीनतेजाः। कच्चित्त्वया प्रीयते चैव विप्र कञ्चित्स्वाध्यायः क्रियते चर्श्यशृङ्ग॥८॥
verses.english: I hope the ascetic merits of the ascetics of this place are on the increase; I hope your father (his spirit) has not become less effulgent. O Brahmana, I hope he is pleased with you. O Rishyashringa, I hope you prosecute the studies which are proper to you.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यशृङ्ग उवाच।
              ऋद्ध्या भवाञ्ज्योतिरिव प्रकाशते मन्ये चाहं त्वामभिवादनीयम्। पाद्यं वै ते संप्रदास्यामि कामाद्यथाधर्मं फलमूलानि चैव॥९॥
verses.english: Rishyashringa said : You are shining with luster like the light. I consider you worthy of obeisance. I shall give you water to wash your feet and also fruits and roots as will be liked by you according to my religious ordinance.

verses.sanskrit: कौश्यां बृस्यामास्स्व यथापजाष कृष्णाजिनेनावृतायां सुखायाम्। क्व चाश्रमस्तव किं नाम चेदं व्रतं ब्रह्मंश्चरसि हि देववत्त्वम्॥१०॥
verses.english: Please to take your seat at your pleasure on this mat made of Kusha grass and covered with the skin of black deer and thus made comfortable to sit upon. Where is your hermitage? What is the name of this Brahma and celestials like VOW which you are observing?

verses.sanskrit:
वेश्योवाच।
              ममाश्रमः काश्यपपुत्र रम्यस्त्रियोजनं शैलमिमं परेण। तत्र स्वधर्मो नाभिवादनं मे न चोदकं पाद्यमुपस्पृशामि॥११॥
verses.english: The Courtesan said : On son of Kashyapa, my charming hermitage is situated three yojanas off from this place on the other side of this mountain. My religious ordinance is not to accept obeisance, nor do I touch water to wash my feet.
verses.bhavadeepa: कौश्यां बृस्यामास्वकुशासने उपविश । यथोपजोषं यथासुखम् । सुखायां सुखकर्याम् ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit: भवता नाभिवाद्योऽहमभिवाद्यो भवान्मया। व्रतमेतादृशं ब्रह्मन्परिष्वज्यो भवान्मया॥१२॥
verses.english: O Brahmana, I do not deserve to receive obeisance from you, but I must make obeisance to you. This is the vow observed by me, namely you must embrace me.

verses.sanskrit:
ऋश्यशृङ्ग उवाच।
              फलानि पक्वानि ददानि तेऽहं भल्लातकान्यामलकानि चैव। करूषकानीङ्गुदधन्वनानि पिप्पलानां कामकारं कुरुष्व॥१३॥
verses.english: Rishyashringa said : I give you ripe fruits such as gall-nuts, myrobalus, Karusas, Ingudas and figs. Be pleased to enjoy them.

verses.sanskrit:
लोमश उवाच।
              सा तानि सर्वाणि विवर्जयित्वा भक्ष्याण्यनर्हाणि ददौ ततोऽस्य। तान्पृश्यशृङ्गस्य महारसानि भृशं सुरूपाणि रुचिं ददुर्हि॥१४॥
verses.english: Lomasha said: Having thrown aside all those (fruits), she gave him food which was not proper to eat. They were exceedingly beautiful and nice and they were very acceptable to Rishyashringa.

verses.sanskrit: ददौ च माल्यानि सुगन्धवन्ति चित्राणि वासांसि च भानुमन्ति। पेयानि चाग्र्याणि ततो मुमोद चिक्रीड चैव प्रजहास चैव॥१५॥
verses.english: She gave him sweet fragrant garlands and various shining cloths. She then gave him strong drinks, she then played, laughed and enjoyed herself.

verses.sanskrit: सा कन्दुकेनारमतास्य मूले विभज्यमाना फलिता लतेव। गात्रैश्च गात्राणि निषेवमाणा समाश्लिषच्चासकृदृश्यशृङ्गम्॥१६॥
verses.english: She played before him with a ball like a broken creeper bent with fruits. She touched his body with her own and she again and again clasped Rishyashringa with her arins.

verses.sanskrit: सर्जानशोकांस्तिलकांश्च वृक्षान्सुपुष्पितानवनाम्यावभज्य। विलज्जमानेव मदाभिभूता प्रलोभयामास सुतं महर्षेः॥१७॥
verses.english: She then bent and broke the flowery twigs from trees, such as the Shala, Ashoka and Tilaka; assuming a bashful look, she tempted the Rishis' son who was over-powered with intoxication.
verses.bhavadeepa: मूले समीपे । विभज्यमाना अङ्गमोटनादीनि कुर्वाणा । निषेवमाणा सूचीवदभ्यन्तरं प्रविशन्ती। ‘षिवु तन्तुसंताने’ इति धातुः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: अथर्श्यशृङ्गं विकृतं समीक्ष्य पुनः पुनः पीड्य च कायमस्य। अवेक्ष्यमाणा शनकैर्जगाम कृत्वाग्निहोत्रस्य तदापदेशम्॥१८॥
verses.english: Having seen Rishyashringa over-powered, she again and again pressed him with her body. Casting glances she slowly went away, as if she was going to make offerings to the holy fire.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यां गतायां मदनेन मत्तो विचेतनश्चाभवदृश्यशृङ्गः। तामेव भावेन गतेन शून्ये विनिःश्वसन्नार्तरूपो बभूव॥१९॥
verses.english: On her departure Rishyashringa became over-powered with desire and became senseless. He became full of her and he felt vacancy. Sighing again and again he seemed to be in great distress.
verses.bhavadeepa: कायं देहं पीड्य आलिंङ्गनेन निपीड्य । अपदेशं छलम् ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit: ततो मुहूर्ताद्धरिपिङ्गलाक्षः प्रवेष्टितो रोमभिरानखाग्रात्। स्वाध्यायवान्वृत्तसमाधियुक्तो विभाण्डकः काश्यपः प्रादुरासीत्॥२०॥
verses.english: At that moment appeared the son of Kashyapa, Vibhandaka whose eyes were as tawny as those of a lion, whose body was covered with hair down to the nails of his foot, who was engaged in his proper studies and whose life was pure and passed in religious meditations.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽपश्यदासीनमुपेत्य पुत्रं ध्यायन्तमेकं विपरीतचित्तम्। विनिःश्वसन्तं मुहुरूर्ध्वदृष्टिं विभाण्डकः पुत्रमुवाच दीनम्॥२१॥
verses.english: He came up and saw his son seated alone, pensive and sad and dejected. He was sighing again and again with upturned eyes. Vibhandaka thus spoke to his distressed son, "O child, why do you not hew logs for the sacrificial fire? I hope you have performed today the Agnihotra (fire sacrifice). I hope you have polished the sacrificial ladles and spoons and brought out the sacrificial cow with her calf, O son, you are not in your wonted state today. You are pensive and absent minded. Why are you so much distressed today? I ask you, who came here today?

verses.sanskrit: न कल्प्यन्ते समिधः किं नु तात कच्चिद्धुतं चाग्निहोत्रं त्वयाद्य। सुनिर्णिक्तं स्रुक्स्रुवं होमधेनुः कच्चित्सवत्साद्य कृता त्वया च॥२२॥
न वै यथापूर्वमिवासि पुत्र चिन्तापरश्चासि विचेतनश्च। दीनोऽतिमात्रं त्वमिहाद्य किं तु पृच्छामि त्वां क इहाद्यागतोऽभूत्॥२३॥
verses.bhavadeepa: कल्प्यन्ते सिद्धाः क्रियन्ते । निर्णिक्तं प्रक्षालितम् । सवत्सा कृता दोहनायेति शेषः ॥२२॥
